## HueMux v0.0.5-alpha.1 — Reach the UI by name *and* by address

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI, not exercised on real hardware here
> beyond a single LAN deployment. Until now a HueMux instance was reachable by
> exactly one name: whatever `listen.host` said. Everything else — the
> address, the machine's hostname, a reverse proxy's vhost — was rejected at
> the WebSocket handshake. The page loaded and then sat there with no lights,
> which is a symptom that looks like a broken bridge and is not one.

### The address and the name now work at the same time

The Origin check accepts any address this machine actually holds, whatever
`listen.host` is set to. Previously that was true only when bound to a
wildcard, so the two ways of deploying were mutually exclusive: bind to a name
and the address stopped working; bind to the address and the name did.

This matters when clients use different DNS. A phone on the LAN resolves the
vhost name; a machine on a VPN only has the address. Both are the same server
and both now work — no setting required.

### `allowed_hosts`

A name HueMux cannot derive — a reverse proxy's vhost, a MagicDNS name — goes
in a new `allowed_hosts` list:

```jsonc
{
  "listen": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 7654 },
  "allowed_hosts": ["huemux.lan"]
}
```

`--allowed-hosts=huemux.lan,other.lan` sets it for one run. A pasted URL is
accepted and reduced to its host, so `"https://huemux.lan:7654/"` is the same
entry. The current list is reported by `GET /api/config` and can be changed
from the settings endpoint.

### Still not a wildcard

The list is an enumeration, and every entry admits exactly one name. A page
from anywhere else is refused whether or not the list is empty, and the check
still runs even when a token is configured — an attacker's page would happily
send a token it had obtained.

Accepting this machine's own addresses is not a widening of trust: a hostile
page can put a foreign *name* in `Origin`, because a name is whatever its
author registered, but it cannot make the browser write an address literal
this machine holds.

### Also in this release

- `Config` contains a slice, so it is no longer comparable with `==`. Tests
  that compared whole configs use `reflect.DeepEqual`.
- Error messages for an unusable `allowed_hosts` entry name the offending
  value, so a typo stops startup instead of silently never matching.
